rows.jp: 彼女はいつも一人だった。

ghs.en: That girl was always alone.

rows.jp: 親族や使用人の誰とも、交わろうとはしなかった。
rows.en: She would associate with neither relatives nor servants.

ghs.en:
She had no desire to mingle with anybody, neither
the relatives nor the employees.

rows.jp: 孤高の君―――

ghs.en: You who stand above---
ghs.assessment: 孤高の君 is the private epithet Taichi gives the aloof, solitary girl. 'You who stand above' turns it into direct address and fails to function as a title.

highlights.text: You who stand above---

rows.jp: 俺は、彼女を内心でそう呼んでいた。
rows.en: That was what I privately called her.

ghs.en:
That is what I called her in my innermost
thoughts.

rows.jp: 言葉をかわしたことはない。
rows.en: We had never exchanged a word.

ghs.en: There had never been exchange of words.
ghs.assessment: The two had never exchanged words. 'There had never been exchange of words' omits an article and both participants.

highlights.text: There had never been exchange of words.

rows.jp: 気にはなっていた。

ghs.en: My interest had been piqued.

rows.jp: 屋敷がどのような人々によって維持され、いかなる経緯をたどってこの有様になったのか、俺は知らない。
rows.en: I don’t know who kept the estate running, or how it had come to be that way.

ghs.en:
I don't know what kind of people maintain the
mansion or how, or even the particulars of how
things were made to be the way they were.

rows.jp: ただそこは、時の流れから隔絶された楽園のごとき場所だった。
rows.en: But it was like a paradise set apart from time.

ghs.en:
Just that this place was like Eden, separated
from the flow of time.

rows.jp: 住むのもまた、浮世離れした人々で。
rows.en: The people who lived there seemed to belong to another world, too.

rows.jp: ときおり俺は彼女らに招かれ、甘い飲み物を振る舞われた。
rows.en: Sometimes the ladies invited me in and served me sweet drinks.

rows.jp: 着飾り、茶を楽しみ、人を招き、散策し。
rows.en: They dressed up, enjoyed their tea, entertained guests, went for walks.

rows.jp: 毎月頭には大量の書物・衣類・嗜好品が届けられた。
rows.en: At the start of every month, great quantities of books, clothing, and luxuries arrived.

rows.jp: 広い庭。
庭師という人々もいた。
rows.en: There were people called gardeners too.

rows.jp: 人里離れ、地代が安いことを差し引いても、なお広漠(こうばく)たるものがあった。
rows.en: Even allowing for how cheap land was so far from any town, the grounds were immense.

ghs.en:
Even taking into account that land rent was cheap
and that it was distant from human populated
areas, it was still almost boundlessly huge.

rows.jp: 小さな俺にとって、お屋敷は広大無辺(こうだいむへん)な世界そのものだったのだ。
rows.en: To the little boy I was then, the estate was the whole world—vast and without end.

ghs.en:
For me, small back then, the residence was the
whole infinitely wide world itself.

rows.jp: 実際、屋敷時代以前の記憶はない。
rows.en: Indeed, I remembered nothing from before my life there.

ghs.en:
In truth, I have no memories of a time before
the mansion.

rows.jp: 世界と屋敷は同じ大きさだった。
rows.en: The world and the estate were the same size.

ghs.en: The world and the mansion had the same huge size.

rows.jp: ある頃からか、俺はご婦人がたに気に入られるようになった。
rows.en: At some point, the ladies began to favor me.

rows.jp: 女のような顔をしている、とのこと。
rows.en: They said I had a girl’s face.

rows.jp: また間近で見るとわかる不思議な模様を描く瞳も、彼女たちを退屈させなかった。
rows.en: The strange patterns visible in my eyes at close range also kept them entertained.

rows.jp: 少女の着るような（それもとりわけ華美な）ドレスを着させられた。
rows.en: They dressed me in the sort of gowns girls wore—especially extravagant ones.

rows.jp: そしてお茶の相手。
rows.en: And made me their companion at tea.

rows.jp: 子供にお茶の味などわからない。
rows.en: A child knows nothing of tea.

ghs.en: Children don't understand the flavor of tea.

rows.jp: でもつきあった。
砂糖菓子めいて甘やかな人々に対し、逆らうという選択肢はなかった。
rows.en: Saying no to these people, sweet as sugar candy, wasn’t an option.

rows.jp: ……少なくともイヤではなかった。
rows.en: ...At least I did not dislike it.

rows.jp: 退屈ではあったけど、楽だったから。
rows.en: It was dull, but it was easy.

rows.jp: こうして幼い子供らに馬乗りにされ髪引かれる玩具の身分から離れた俺は、新しい仕事として人形をすることになった。
rows.en: The little children no longer rode me or pulled my hair. My new job was to be a doll.

rows.jp: そんな俺を、彼女……孤高の君はひややかな視線で見ていた。
rows.en: And she—the Solitary Lady—watched me with a cold gaze.

rows.jp: いや、見てさえいなかった。
rows.en: No. She didn’t even look at me.

rows.jp: 興味がないらしく、視線はいつも俺を素通りしていった。
rows.en: Uninterested, her gaze always passed straight through me.

ghs.en:
Her sight always passed through me as if I simply
did not exist, as if there was no interest in me.

rows.jp: 支倉曜子。

ghs.en: Hasekura Youko,

rows.jp: 末娘。

ghs.en: youngest of the girls there.
ghs.assessment: 末娘 identifies Youko as the youngest daughter. 'Youngest of the girls there' omits the family relation.

highlights.text: youngest of the girls there.

rows.jp: ただ家族からは、それほど可愛がられている様子はない。
rows.en: But her family didn’t seem especially fond of her.

ghs.en: There wasn't that much affection from her family.

rows.jp: むしろ疎んじられていた。

ghs.en: More like, she was being shunned.

rows.jp: なるほど確かに彼女は、なかば夢幻の住人であるご婦人がたとは、違う世界に生きていた。
rows.en: She really did belong to a different world from those ladies, who lived half in dreams.

ghs.en:
I see, it's certain, she lives in a different
world from that of the ladies that half-dwell
in fantasy.

rows.jp: ……現実という世界に。

ghs.en: ...in the world called reality.

rows.jp: 一度、掃除の人夫として駆り出されたことがある。
rows.en: Once, I was drafted into a cleaning crew.

ghs.en:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.
ghs.assessment: Taichi was once pressed into service as cleaning labor. 'Was tossed out when I was working as a cleaning man' instead says that he was ejected or dismissed.

highlights.text:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.

rows.jp: 人形ハジメマシタ、以前のことだ。
rows.en: This was before I went into the doll business.

ghs.en: It was before the Time of the Doll had begun,

rows.jp: 使用人さんたちにまじって参加した。

ghs.en: when I was mingling with the servitude.
ghs.assessment: Taichi joins the household servants in the cleaning. 'Mingling with the servitude' uses an abstract condition of bondage instead of the people.

highlights.text: when I was mingling with the servitude.

rows.jp: 通いの人間は使わない方針だったためか、人手の貸し借りは茶飯事だった。
rows.en: Maybe it was because they only hired live-in help, but staff were constantly being borrowed for other jobs.

ghs.en:
Perhaps because there was a policy to avoid
using people who don't live in the house, lending
and borrowing of manpower was a common thing.

rows.jp: 十時と三時にお茶の休憩を一時間ずつ挟みながら、順番に部屋を掃除していく。
rows.en: With hour-long tea breaks at ten and three, we cleaned the rooms in order.

ghs.en:
I cleaned the rooms one after the other. It was
an unhurried, well-paced job that also had
one-hour tea breaks at ten and at three.

rows.jp: 夕方には彼女の部屋に辿り着いた。

ghs.en: At evening's dusk I had finally reached her room.

rows.jp: はじめて彼女の声を聞いた。
rows.en: I heard her voice for the first time.

ghs.en: I heard her voice for the very first time.

rows.jp: 『……ここはいいわ』

ghs.en: Youko: 『...no need here.』

rows.jp: 短くそっけない。

ghs.en: Short and brusque.

rows.jp: 機能的。

ghs.en: Efficient.

rows.jp: けど、蠱惑的だった。

ghs.en: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.
ghs.assessment: 蠱惑的 calls the voice bewitching or seductively captivating. 'Captivating as magic' turns the quality into a simile and loses its alluring register.

highlights.text: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.

rows.jp: ちらりと見た室内は、とても乙女の部屋とは思えない。
rows.en: The glimpse I caught inside was nothing like a girl’s bedroom.

ghs.en:
A fleeting glance inside her room showed me
something that did not make me think of a
maiden's room at all.

rows.jp: 数台のパソコン。
四方の壁を覆い隠す本棚と、そこに収まりきらず床に堆(うずたか)く積まれた書物。
rows.en: Bookshelves concealing every wall, and books stacked high on the floor when the shelves overflowed.

rows.jp: 重々しい工作台と、真新しい工具。
rows.en: A massive workbench and gleaming new tools.

rows.jp: かなり広い私室は雑多な知識と技術で埋め尽くされていて、秘密基地を連想させた。
rows.en: Her large room was crammed with all kinds of knowledge and technology. It reminded me of a secret base.

rows.jp: なるほど確かに一人だけ異質な者が、異世界にはいたのだ。
rows.en: So even that other world had one outsider.

rows.jp: 綺麗な衣装を着て、女の子の言葉遣いでお茶の相手をしている時、支倉曜子について問いかけたことがある。
rows.en: Once, while dressed prettily and speaking like a girl over tea, I asked about Youko Hasekura.

ghs.en:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.
ghs.assessment: Taichi wears beautiful clothes while speaking in girlish language. 'Gaudy dress' adds a negative judgment not present in 綺麗.

highlights.text:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.

rows.jp: もの静かな老婦人は答えた。

ghs.en: A very quiet older lady replied,

rows.jp: 末の息子のそのまた娘と。
rows.en: She was the daughter of the youngest son.

ghs.en:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.
ghs.assessment: Youko is the daughter of the youngest son. The English adds another generation, making her the daughter of the son of the Head's son.

highlights.text:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.

rows.jp: 若く快活な婦人は答えた。

ghs.en: A younger and cheerful adult lady replied,

rows.jp: 望まれて生まれた娘ではないと。
rows.en: She was not a wanted child.

ghs.en: that she was a daughter born unwanted.

rows.jp: 姦しい三姉妹は囀(さえず)った。

ghs.en: Three boisterous sisters chirped,

rows.jp: 若旦那とうら若き使用人との秘められた恋物語と、その顛末。
rows.en: The secret romance between the young master and a youthful servant, and how it ended.

rows.jp: 誰にもなつかず愛を知らない娘の咎と、訪れるであろう悲劇的結末。
rows.en: The sins of a girl who grew close to no one and knew nothing of love, and the tragic end that surely awaited her.

rows.jp: 支倉の血でありながら支倉の一員ではない、そんな汚点に対する奥ゆかしい嘆き。
rows.en: Their genteel lament for the stain who bore Hasekura blood without belonging to Hasekura.

rows.jp: 要するに忌み子だったのだ。
rows.en: In short, she was an accursed child.

rows.jp: 誰も彼女に語りかける者はなく、彼女もまた誰にも語らなかった。
rows.en: No one spoke to her, and she spoke to no one.

rows.jp: 腫れ物だった。
rows.en: She was a wound everyone feared to touch.

ghs.en: She was a tumor.
ghs.assessment: 腫れ物 figuratively means a sore spot or untouchable person whom everyone handles warily. 'She was a tumor' literalizes the image into a medical growth.

highlights.text: She was a tumor.

rows.jp: 彼女の実父である若旦那なる人物は、海外に留学してしまったそうだ。
rows.en: The young master, her biological father, had reportedly gone abroad to study.

ghs.en:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.
ghs.assessment: The narrator reports that her father had gone abroad to study. 'Seemed to be studying abroad' makes the study contemporaneous rather than the departure a past fact.

highlights.text:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.

rows.jp: 母親の使用人は……亡くなっていた。
rows.en: Her mother, the servant... was dead.

ghs.en: The servant, her mother... had passed away.

rows.jp: 何者にもなれない少女。
rows.en: A girl who could never be anyone.

rows.jp: 誰にも求められない少女。
rows.en: A girl wanted by no one.

rows.jp: 傷つく？
否。傷つかない。
支倉曜子は強かった。
意に介さなかった。
たぶん気づいたいたんだと思う。
世界が箱庭であることを。
rows.en: That the world was a miniature garden.

rows.jp: 人形生活の合間、図書室に通った。
rows.en: Between sessions as a doll, I visited the library.

rows.jp: 影響を受けたのかも知れない。
貴婦人からは作法とお茶を学んだ。
rows.en: From the ladies I learned manners and tea.

rows.jp: けれど知恵と技術と真実は、そこにはなかった。
rows.en: But there was no wisdom there, no skill, no truth.

ghs.en: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.
ghs.assessment: The ladies offered neither wisdom, technical skill, nor truth. 'Art' is too broad for 技術 here, and 'there weren't' is inverted ungrammatically.

highlights.text: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.

rows.jp: 補うために、使う者の少ない図書室に通い詰めた。
rows.en: To make up for that, I haunted the little-used library.

ghs.en:
To supplement, I frequently visited the rarely
populated library.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんとはよく出会った。

ghs.en: I met Youko-chan frequently,

rows.jp: 依然として会話はない。

ghs.en: yet still without conversation.

rows.jp: なんとなく癪(しゃく)だったので、俺からアプローチすることもなかった。
rows.en: That irritated me for some reason, so I made no effort to approach her either.

ghs.en:
For some annoyance or another, there was no
approach from me either.

rows.jp: 好ましくは思っていたけど、仲良くなりたいと願いはしなかった。
rows.en: I liked her, but I didn’t want to be friends.

ghs.en:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.
ghs.assessment: Taichi thought well of Youko or found her likable. 'Desirable' introduces a stronger sexualized evaluation.

highlights.text:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.

rows.jp: 俺の美的傾向は、この頃から確立されたようだ。
rows.en: My aesthetic tastes seem to have taken shape around then.

ghs.en:
Seems that my aesthetic sensitivity was formed
right around that time.

rows.jp: なんというか……自立しているものに惹かれた。
rows.en: How should I put it... I was drawn to things that could stand on their own.

ghs.en:
How to say this... I was attracted, charmed, by
what can stand on its own.

rows.jp: 独力で生きるものと、力に。
rows.en: Beings that lived by their own strength—and strength itself.

ghs.en:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.
ghs.assessment: He is drawn to beings that live by their own power and to that power itself. 'By that strength' makes the strength an agent or means acting on him.

highlights.text:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.

rows.jp: 知識にしろ技術にしろ、そういう側面がある。
rows.en: Knowledge and skill have that quality, too.

ghs.en:
Whether it's in the knowledge or whether it's in
the craft, that side of things exists.

rows.jp: 人は群れる。

ghs.en: Humans flock together.

rows.jp: 群れることを渇望する。

ghs.en: They crave flocking itself.

rows.jp: そして同時に、聖域を持とうとする。
rows.en: At the same time, they seek a sanctuary.

ghs.en:
And then, simultaneously, they want to have a holy
ground, a sanctuary.

rows.jp: 侵害されない自分のための場所を欲する。
rows.en: A place of their own that cannot be violated.

ghs.en:
They desire a place for themselves that
is never infringed.

rows.jp: しかし人と接すれば境界線は揺らぐ。
rows.en: But contact with others makes the boundaries shift.

ghs.en:
Yet when people come into contact, the boundary
lines waver.

rows.jp: 領土は減ったり増えたりする。

ghs.en:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.
ghs.assessment: Personal territory shrinks and expands as boundaries shift. 'Maybe decreases, maybe increases' changes the general dynamic into uncertainty.

highlights.text:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.

rows.jp: 不快。
矛盾。
一般的な価値観では、千の軍隊より一人の英雄が好まれる。
rows.en: By ordinary standards, a single hero is preferable to a thousand armies.

rows.jp: 単一の絶対者。英雄。
rows.en: The single absolute being. The hero.

rows.jp: 人の望むもの。
憧れという形をとった、願望に過ぎない。
rows.en: Nothing more than a wish in the guise of admiration.

rows.jp: 一人で生きたいのか、群れて生きたいのか……人はそのどちらにもＹＥＳと答えることができる。
rows.en: Do people want to live alone, or among the herd? They can answer yes to both.

rows.jp: 閑話休題。
図書室では、彼女の読んだ本を追って読んだ。
rows.en: In the library, I read the books she’d read.

rows.jp: 憧れから。

ghs.en: Because of this aspiration.

rows.jp: あるいは少女の完璧さへの嫉妬から。
rows.en: Or jealousy of the girl’s perfection.

ghs.en:
Or, perhaps, because of jealousy for her
perfection.
ghs.assessment: One feels jealousy 'of' or 'over' another's perfection. 'Jealousy for her perfection' suggests jealousy on its behalf.

highlights.text:
Or, perhaps, because of jealousy for her
perfection.

rows.jp: 書物の内容は高度過ぎてほとんどわからなかった。
rows.en: They were too advanced. I understood almost nothing.

ghs.en:
The subjects of the book were extremely advanced,
and I just about didn't understand them,
ghs.assessment: The books' content was so advanced that Taichi understood almost none of it. 'Just about didn't understand' can imply that he narrowly avoided failing to understand and is unidiomatic here.

highlights.text:
The subjects of the book were extremely advanced,
and I just about didn't understand them,

rows.jp: けど読み続けた。

ghs.en: yet I kept reading.

rows.jp: 図書室では何百回となく出会い、すれ違った。
rows.en: We crossed paths in that library hundreds of times.

ghs.en:
We met in the library so many hundreds of times,
just passing by each other, never meeting.
ghs.assessment: They encountered and passed one another hundreds of times. The English first says they met and then contradicts it with 'never meeting.'

highlights.text:
We met in the library so many hundreds of times,
just passing by each other, never meeting.

rows.jp: 一度の会話もない空間を、俺たちは共有し続けた。
rows.en: We went on sharing that space without a single word passing between us.

ghs.en:
We co-owned that air that never once we filled
with conversation.
ghs.assessment: They continued to share a space in which they never once spoke. 'Co-owned that air that never once we filled' is a strained and ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text:
We co-owned that air that never once we filled
with conversation.

rows.jp: そういう時代が、数年間続いた。
rows.en: So it went for several years.

ghs.en: And that era continued for several years.

rows.jp: で、だ。

ghs.en: And then.

rows.jp: 楽園には崩壊がつきもの。
rows.en: Paradise always comes with a fall.

rows.jp: これは人類最初の楽園からしてそうだから、避けようのない摂理と考えられる。
rows.en: It had been true since humanity’s first paradise. Apparently it was an inescapable law.

rows.jp: 具体的には、屋敷のご当主である支倉氏の急激なる凋落によって。
rows.en: In our case, it was the sudden downfall of the Hasekura patriarch.

rows.jp: 悲劇のはじまりだった。
支倉のお上品な人々はいなくなった。
使用人たちは残された。
支倉のかわりに入ってきたのは、新興の人物とその親類縁者だった。
rows.en: In their place came an upstart and all his relations.

rows.jp: 粗暴な人々であった。

ghs.en: We met wild, rude, violent people.
ghs.assessment: The newcomers were a brutish lot. 'We met ... people' invents an encounter and makes the narrator's group the subject.

highlights.text: We met wild, rude, violent people.

rows.jp: 老若男女、揃ってやってきた。
rows.en: Old and young, men and women, they came together.

ghs.en: Men and women, young and old, all alike,

rows.jp: 全員が、腐肉あさりの素質を持っていた。
rows.en: They all had the instincts of carrion scavengers.

ghs.en:
all of them to the last had the makings
of carrion eaters.

rows.jp: 三日経たないうちに、使用人の一人が暴行された。
rows.en: Within three days, one servant was assaulted.

ghs.en:
Three days hadn't passed and one of the servants
was assaulted.

rows.jp: 事件である。

ghs.en: A matter for investigation,

rows.jp: けれどここは箱庭だった。
rows.en: But this was a miniature garden.

ghs.en: however, this was a miniature garden.

rows.jp: 閉鎖された空間。

ghs.en: This space was sealed.

rows.jp: 独自の秩序が発生した。

ghs.en: It had originated its own order.

rows.jp: 広大な土地に囲まれた屋敷ともなれば、治外法権に近い。
rows.en: Surrounded by all that land, the estate was practically beyond the reach of the law.

ghs.en:
When a mansion is surrounded by a vast plot of
land, it is nearly extraterritorial.

rows.jp: 日々、どんな饗宴が繰り広げられたか。
rows.en: What kind of feasts did they hold there, day after day?

ghs.en:
And what kind of feast would unfold there,
day after day?

rows.jp: 屋敷の一室は、もとは夜会に用いられていたホールだった。
rows.en: One chamber had originally been a ballroom.

ghs.en:
One of the room of the mansion was, originally,
used for evening parties.
ghs.assessment: The singular subject requires 'One of the rooms,' not 'One of the room.'

highlights.text:
One of the room of the mansion was, originally,
used for evening parties.

rows.jp: 支倉の人たちは、ちょっとしたパーティーが大好きで、よく使用されたものだ。
rows.en: The Hasekuras loved little parties and used it often.

ghs.en:
The people of the Hasekura family really loved
their little events, so it was used quite
frequently.

rows.jp: 粗暴な人々は、ここを別の夜会に用いた。
rows.en: The brutes used it for another kind of evening party.
